notes.summary: All-cone, all-Reeb finite-energy target criterion: finite explicit FS dual energy is equivalent to integrating every actual E1 potential, is independent of the Reeb field on K, and is necessary for genuine MA outputs. This is a target-class theorem, not image sufficiency.
notes.detailedSummary: Using only the explicitly accepted full P13.1 mathematical theorem as a supporting premise, the actual reference MA is the trivial-valuation Dirac probability. Fixed-ray mixed-product expansion gives J(tu)≤2^n t²J(u) for normalized actual E1 potentials. A decreasing convex-series argument and this bound prove the converse integrability criterion. The FS, CPSH and E1 dual suprema coincide. Raw decreasing target integrals are continuous even for nonmetrizable carriers and arbitrary nets. Tangency proves finite dual energy and optimality for every genuine output. No envelope property, nonlinear strong transport or inverse existence is used.
notes.text:
This note proves a partial theorem over every algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, on every normal good polarized affine cone of dimension n≥1 and every Reeb field ξ, including irrational fields. Put p=n−1 and K=X0^T. All potentials are the actual cone classes restricted to K. The reference ρξ vanishes on K. The supporting mathematical premise is the explicitly accepted FULL P13.1 proof bound at /workspace/research/deliverables/original-P13.1/P13.1-reviewed-argument.md, SHA256 de75b9ae55fbeb63c605505a328ed306c321a8e674331827cde51f5cfad76609. The canonical notes and operational preservation assertions are not separate mathematical premises. The accepted theorem gives actual-class convexity, fixed-field decreasing energy and weighted mixed-MA continuity, positive mixed probabilities, integration by parts and Hodge index, intrinsic raw root bijections with normalized E1 transport, and the canonical outer derivative. It does not give envelope attainment, actual E1 completeness or an inverse.

The actual probability is νξ(u1,…,up)=Vξ^(−1)ddc u1⋯ddc up ddc ρξ^+, and Eξ(u)=(nVξ)^(−1)Σ_(j=0)^p∫K u(ddc u)^j(ddc ρξ)^(p−j)ddc ρξ^+. Finite-energy versions use genuine same-field decreasing limits. At a rational field η=sηe, with the effective supported gcd-one grading and the actual degree-d Veronese cover, the accepted normal quotient has dimension p, Vη=s^(−n)d^(1−n)(Ld^p), ωη=Ld/(sd), ωη^p=sVη, Eη=E_Ld/(sd). Single-degree Hilbert coefficients are (Ld^p)/p!, cutoff coefficients Vη/n!, and the signed full-ring bridge is E=(n+1)S/n. These factors retain one radial unit mass, one finite-map degree d and n factors 1/(sd).

The reference measure is δ_vtriv. Rationally its canonical zero-weight product model on the normal integral quotient has one central component of multiplicity one, mixed intersection Ld^p and hence one trivial-valuation probability mass. The accepted radial lift gives vtriv on K. At an irrational field, only the bounded references move; their local uniform convergence and the accepted genuine bounded current limit give the same Dirac mass. For an actual nontrivial PSH potential, supK u=u(vtriv) is finite. Normalize u(vtriv)=0, so u≤0 and J(u)=−E(u).

Define Lξ(μ)=sup_(w∈H(ξ))[Eξ(w)−∫K w dμ] for a Radon probability μ on K. These are explicit finite primary homogeneous FS tests, not unknown outputs or inverse potentials. Uniform FS approximation and genuine energy continuity equate the supremum with CPSH. For a decreasing bounded-above usc net h_i↓h on compact Hausdorff K, ∫h_i dμ↓∫h dμ: Radon regularity expresses a usc integral as an infimum over continuous majorants; for any continuous g≥h, the increasing open sets {h_i<g+ε} cover K, so compactness and directedness give h_i≤g+ε eventually. Infimize and let ε tend to zero. This proves the net assertion, including extended integrals.

If Lξ(μ)<∞ and u_i↓u is an actual CPSH defining net of u∈E1, then ∫u_i dμ≥E(u_i)−L. Passing through the two decreasing continuities proves ∫u dμ≥E(u)−L>−∞. Potentials are bounded above, so they are L1. Taking the limit of E(u_i)−∫u_i proves Lξ(μ)=sup_(u∈E1)[E(u)−∫u dμ]=Eξ^∨(μ). When the bounded-test supremum is infinite, the E1 supremum is infinite as well.

For the converse, let b_l=−∫u dνξ(u repeated l times,ρ repeated p−l times) for a normalized E1 potential. All b_l are finite nonnegative, b_0=0 by the reference Dirac, and J(u)=Σb_l/n. On the actual segment u_t=tu+(1−t)ρ, 0≤t≤1, positive mixed-product expansion gives J(u_t)=(1/n)Σ_(l=1)^p[tΣ_(j=l)^p binom(j,l)t^l(1−t)^(j−l)]b_l≤2^n t²J(u). The bound uses t^(l+1)≤t² and Σ_(j=l)^p binom(j,l)=binom(n,l+1)≤2^n. It passes to E1 by genuine fixed-field decreasing continuity. No cross-ray linear axioms are inferred from roots.

Suppose all actual E1 potentials are μ-integrable. There is B<∞ with ∫(−u)dμ≤B on the normalized class J(u)≤1. Otherwise choose such u_j with integrals ≥2^j. The actual convex restrictions w_m=Σ_(j=1)^m2^(−j)u_j, with remaining reference weight, decrease, are zero at vtriv and have E(w_m)≥−1 by concavity. Their nontrivial actual PSH limit w has E(w)≥−1 by decreasing continuity, but ∫(−w)dμ=∞ by monotone convergence, a contradiction. For J(u)≥2^(−n), choose t=(2^nJ(u))^(−1/2); the segment bound and the uniform integral bound give ∫(−u)dμ≤B√(2^nJ(u)). For smaller J the bound B applies. Therefore Lξ(μ)≤B+2^(n−2)B²<∞. This proves the intrinsic finite-energy TARGET criterion Lξ(μ)<∞ iff E1(ξ)⊂L1(μ). It does not prove that every such target is in the image.

The accepted normalized roots are onto E1 and satisfy u/c≤Rξηu≤u/C≤0 with c,C>0 controlling all supported degrees. Integrability of all source potentials therefore implies integrability of every target potential; the inverse gives the converse. Thus the finite-energy measure class is independent of Reeb field on the same K. This gives no strong-topology transport.

Finally concavity and first variation on an actual fixed-ray segment give E(w)≤E(u)+∫(w−u)dMA(u). Raw decreasing approximation and accepted weighted continuity give this inequality for E1. For ν=MA(u), it implies Lξ(ν)=E(u)−∫u dν<∞, with equality obtained by using u as an E1 test. This establishes necessity and genuine optimality. The printed opposite inequality at Wu2406.13684v1 LF1249 is not a premise.

For later use, the accepted outer functional is F(g)=sup_{w∈CPSH,w≤g}E(w), F↓(h)=inf_{g∈C(K),g≥h}F(g). It agrees with actual PSH energy and is decreasing-net continuous. One fixed dense lattice D⊂C(K) has actual auxiliary slope-A representatives f=a−b, a/A,b/A∈CPSH(ξ). For |t|≤τ and every actual E1 u, |F↓(u+tf)−E(u)−t∫f dMA(u)|≤C_f t², C_f=2pA(1+Aτ)^(p−1)||f||; for p=0 the remainder is zero. Each fixed continuous direction follows by uniform approximation. These are exactly the accepted hypotheses used by n2.

Full arguments are P13.2-argument.md Sections 1–3 and P13.2-paper.tex in this workspace. The literal source bodies, hashes and exact LF coordinates are in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. notes.summary: Every finite-energy target on K has genuine FS approximate solutions with quantitative weak error, I-Cauchy potentials and bounded normalized energy. A fixed-ray estimate identifies any actual E1 limit as a solution. Actual completeness remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: Outer duality and both-sign accepted differentiation yield |(MA(u)−μ)(f)|≤d_u/s+C_fs. Choosing FS deficits below j^(−2) gives weak convergence of genuine mass-one measures on any compact Hausdorff K. A reconstructed positive fixed-ray Hessian gives a_p I(u,v)≤E((u+v)/2)−(E(u)+E(v))/2 with a_p=p/4^(p+1), hence I≤(d_u+d_v)/(2a_p). Normalized energies are bounded. Cauchy–Schwarz and mass-A auxiliary products give the genuine MA weak continuity bound √(2Ap||f||I). These results do not realize a formal completion or assert arbitrary nonmonotone target-integration continuity.
notes.text:
Use n1 for the exact actual cone classes, normalization, mixed products, Hodge index, finite dual energy, decreasing target integrability and accepted outer derivative. Fix ξ and a Radon probability μ on K with L=Lξ(μ)<∞. For a genuine u∈E1 define its deficit d_u=L−E(u)+∫u dμ≥0.

For continuous g and a feasible actual CPSH w≤g, positivity of μ gives E(w)−∫g dμ≤E(w)−∫w dμ≤L. Taking the supremum gives F(g)−∫g dμ≤L. If h is bounded-above usc and μ-integrable, approximate h by the decreasing net of all continuous majorants below a fixed upper constant. Minima make that net directed; normality of compact Hausdorff K and usc level sets show its infimum is h. The decreasing target-integral fact in n1 and the outer decreasing continuity give F↓(h)−∫h dμ≤L. In particular this holds for h=u+tf, since n1 proves u is μ-integrable.

For f∈D and |t|≤τ, the lower side of the accepted derivative estimate implies t∫f d(MA(u)−μ)≤d_u+C_f t². Use t=s and t=−s to obtain |∫f d(MA(u)−μ)|≤d_u/s+C_f s for 0<s≤τ, C_f=2pA(1+Aτ)^(p−1)||f||. If d_u=0, let s decrease to zero and then use density of D and probability mass one to get MA(u)=μ. The converse follows from n1's tangent identity. This is both-sign Euler–Lagrange at an already genuine potential, not an intrinsic attainment condition used as an image characterization.

By the explicit FS supremum choose u_j∈H(ξ) with d_j<j^(−2), and normalize by constants if desired; MA and deficits are constant invariant. Taking τ=1,s=1/j gives |∫f d(MA(u_j)−μ)|≤(1+C_f)/j for f∈D. For arbitrary continuous f choose f_m∈D uniformly close and add at most 2||f−f_m||, because both measures have mass one. Choose m before j. This proves weak convergence of genuine probabilities on the fixed K, including nonmetrizable K and irrational ξ. Existence of the sequence uses the real supremum; no enumeration of an arbitrary ground field is assumed. Any E1 maximizing net similarly has weakly convergent genuine MA outputs.

There is additional actual potential control. Let p=n−1≥1, z=u−v, and for continuous actual same-field potentials define B_j=−Vξ^(−1)∫z ddc z (ddc u)^j(ddc v)^(p−1−j)ddc ρξ^+≥0, 0≤j≤p−1. The accepted fixed-ray Hodge index gives nonnegativity. Integration by parts and the difference of powers give I(u,v)=∫(u−v)d(MA(v)−MA(u))=ΣB_j. For g(t)=E(v+tz), the actual product expansion gives −g''(t)=pΣ binom(p−1,j)t^j(1−t)^(p−1−j)B_j.

The Green kernel for the midpoint on [0,1] is G(1/2,t)=(1/2)min(t,1−t). Thus H=E((u+v)/2)−(E(u)+E(v))/2=∫G(1/2,t)(−g''(t))dt≥a_p I(u,v), where a_p=p/4^(p+1): on [1/4,3/4] the kernel is ≥1/8, each monomial is ≥4^(−(p−1)), each binomial ≥1, and the interval length is 1/2. All B_j and I are sums of accepted weighted actual mixed measures. Raw simultaneous decreasing CPSH approximation passes nonnegativity, I and this midpoint inequality to E1, without postulating new unbounded currents. The actual midpoint is in E1 by convexity. Its nonnegative deficit equals (d_u+d_v)/2−H, so I(u,v)≤(d_u+d_v)/(2a_p). Every maximizing sequence is therefore I-Cauchy modulo constants.

The reference deficit is L. The two nonnegative tangent deficits between normalized u and the reference sum to I(u,ρ); the reference one is −E(u), since MA(ρ)=δ_vtriv and u(vtriv)=0. Consequently −E(u)≤I(u,ρ)≤(d_u+L)/(2a_p). Normalized maximizing sequences have bounded finite energy. This bound is not potential compactness or actual completeness.

A genuine weak continuity estimate resolves what would happen if an actual limit existed. Represent a fixed f∈D by a−b with actual slope-A psh a,b and a/A,b/A∈CPSH(ξ). For M_j=(ddc u)^j(ddc v)^(p−1−j)ddc ρ^+, fixed-ray Hodge index and Cauchy–Schwarz give |V^(−1)∫f ddc z M_j|≤√(Q_j(f)B_j), Q_j(f)=−V^(−1)∫f ddc f M_j≥0. Since ddc f=ddc a−ddc b, the two positive products involving a or b have mass A after dividing by V: factor out A and use the actual mixed probability for a/A or b/A. Hence Q_j(f)≤2A||f||. Sum the difference-of-powers identity and use Σ√B_j≤√(pΣB_j). This gives |∫f d(MA(u)−MA(v))|≤√(2Ap||f|| I(u,v)). Fixed-field decreasing approximation passes both sides to genuine E1. Uniform approximation of continuous directions gives weak MA continuity whenever I(u_j,u)→0 with an actual E1 u.

Therefore an actual E1/R limit of the maximizing sequence would satisfy MA(u_j)→MA(u) weakly by this estimate and MA(u_j)→μ weakly by the deficit estimate, forcing MA(u)=μ. This is an independent realization reduction through actual completeness. Actual completeness on all normal cones is NOT proved. A formal completion cannot replace the missing potential. The measure-limit route does not require passing target integrals through a nonmonotone maximizing sequence; once a genuine solution exists, n1 already gives its finite target integral and exact optimality. Arbitrary nonmonotone target-integration continuity remains unasserted.

For n=1 the accepted effective normal grading gives R=k[z], K={vtriv}, actual restrictions are constants, E(u)=u(vtriv), and the empty horizontal product with the radial factor gives MA(u)=δ_vtriv. The sole probability has a genuine solution and dual energy zero, unique modulo constants. This special case does not complete the all-dimensional task.

notes.summary: Proved carrier usc-envelope transport across all Reeb fields reduces an envelope route to a rational singular base. That base remains unverified: the public singular v1 lower-growth Proposition 4.19 has an explicit smooth-affine-line counterexample.
notes.detailedSummary: On the torified punctured cone Ω≅K×R, uniform orbit slopes give R(sup u_i)=sup R u_i and R(U*)=(RU)*, including −∞ values. Thus carrier usc-sup stability transfers through the actual raw roots, without implying strong continuity or completeness. Independently, v=(log+|z|)^2 is locally psh by decreasing rational dyadic secants and satisfies the source lower-growth condition g≤v+1/4 for g=log+|z|, but no global decreasing FS sequence can majorize its quadratic growth on the Gauss ray. This disproves the proposition with its printed definition, not the corrected final singular EP conclusion. Corrected growth, regularization/removal, contact, trace, Rossi/Runge, singular induction and arbitrary-field descent are not certified.
notes.text:
Use n1 only for the explicitly accepted actual root maps, cone action, reference and actual-class membership. The next statement proves an analytic usc transport, not just an order assertion. Let Ω be the torified analytic points off the vertex. The accepted action (v+tη)(Σfα)=minα[v(fα)+t⟨η,α⟩] is jointly continuous; each fixed t is a homeomorphism with inverse −t. For homogeneous generators h_i of weights β_i, ρξ(v)=max_i[−v(h_i)/⟨ξ,β_i⟩] is finite continuous off the vertex, and sξ(v)=v+ρξ(v)ξ belongs to K. The maps v↦(sξ(v),ρξ(v)) and (x,r)↦x−rξ are continuous inverses, giving Ω≅K×R. Hence an equivariant extension U(v)=h(sξ(v))+ρξ(v) has usc regularization U*(v)=h*(sξ(v))+ρξ(v), including −∞ values and arbitrary nets.

Take a nonempty family of actual ξ-PSH potentials with a uniform upper bound on K, and U=sup_i u_i on Ω. It is locally bounded above and retains U(v)−Ct≤U(v+tη)≤U(v)−ct for t≥0 with 0<c≤C from all supported degree ratios. U* retains the inequalities by taking usc regularizations and using the fixed-action homeomorphisms. An orbit is either identically −∞ or finite, Lipschitz, strictly decreasing and onto R. Define R U and R U* by their unique zero parameters in the finite case and −∞ in the other case, without claiming new psh membership.

At v set r=sup_i R u_i(v). For t>r the uniform lower slope gives U(v+tη)≤−c(t−r)<0; for t<r some branch is positive. If r=−∞ all source orbits are −∞. Thus R U=sup_i R u_i. Also R U*=(R U)*. To prove the second identity, put r*=R U*(v). For t>r*, U*(v+tη)<0, so a neighborhood has U strictly negative; pull it back by the fixed inverse action to bound nearby R U below t. Conversely, for t<r*, U*(v+tη)>0, so every neighborhood there meets {U>0}; pull back to show every neighborhood of v meets {R U>t}. Arbitrary such t give equality. If r*=−∞, the first argument works for every real t. Local upper bounds exclude +∞.

Define carrier usc-sup stability at ξ by requiring (sup_i u_i|K)* to be the restriction of an actual ξ-PSH potential for every such family. Root images retain a uniform upper bound, since their suprema are their values at vtriv and the orbit slopes bound those values from the original uniform bound. If this property holds at η, apply it to the root family; the preceding identities identify its envelope with R U*. The accepted raw inverse root is an actual ξ-PSH potential and, by its unique zero set and ξ equivariance, equals U* on Ω. Its restriction is the source carrier envelope. Reversing fields proves equivalence at every Reeb field. Actual membership follows from the accepted inverse, not an assumed openness of torification. No envelope on the full noninvariant link or strong continuity of roots is inferred.

For a rational field the accepted actual quotient/torsor and residual torification connect this property to invariant projective envelopes on a normal quotient. An independently proved unrestricted projective EP there would suffice. This singular base is not supplied by order transport. To see that arbitrary normal projective bases occur, take a normal integral projective V and ample Cartier D. Its full section ring is the intersection of k(V)[t] and the Gauss valuation rings giving ft^m the value v_F(f)+m ord_F(D), over prime divisors F. Normality identifies sections by these codimension-one inequalities; the intersection is integrally closed. Ampleness gives finite generation and a high standard Veronese with Proj equal to V. Its scalar-torus normal cone is an original cone and has V as rational quotient, with trivial residual torus. Thus a universal smooth-quotient simplification cannot cover the original family.

There is a concrete obstruction to merely citing the supplied singular source E=Lyuhui Wu, arXiv:2609.27610v1. Its PDF SHA256 is 11808a6c9ede9c0158b27e16700fc180a4ac8df12a4586a7178e1958e8f6bba8; extract SHA256 c8ffe91a631da67f6d3872a1a06ab8d15755aed2f926cdf326725ca3662cef7d. Inclusive one-based LF coordinates use UTF-8 bytes decode then split('\n'). At LF766–768, Definition 3.15(2) requires an FS g with g≤v+O(1), a LOWER-growth condition. At LF769–774 regularizable means a decreasing global FS sequence. Proposition 4.19 LF1560–1562 asserts equality of these classes on smooth affine varieties. Its proof LF1569–1572 asserts the opposite upper bound and invokes Lemma 3.25(1), whose LF952–957 hypothesis already includes regularizability.

The lower-growth proposition is false as printed. On A1 over the original k set v=(max(log|z|,0))² and g=max(log|z|,0), giving both value zero at z=0. The function v is continuous finite and locally psh in the exact Definition 3.8 LF703–707. For any rational M>0, on {|z|<e^M} use t=−log|z| and dyadic secant interpolation of t² on [−M,0], extended by zero for t≥0 including +∞. The rational PL interpolants are convex, finite and continuous; their nonzero affine branches are used on the finite coordinate part, and near +∞ the function is the constant zero. They thus meet the local PL and tropical-convex definitions LF643–700. Nested dyadic refinement decreases the interpolants to (max(−t,0))². Composing with the z tropicalization gives the required decreasing local TConv–PL sequences. These neighborhoods cover the affine analytification. The generator z, rational coefficient 1 and constant branch zero make g an actual source-FS function. For r≥0, r≤r²+1/4, so g≤v+1/4 everywhere: v is in the printed lower-growth class.

On the Gauss seminorm of radius e^t, t≥0, every nonzero f∈k[z] has log|f|=(deg f)t by trivial valuation of coefficients. Any source-FS function is a finite maximum of positive rational multiples of such logarithms plus rational constants and a constant branch. It is ≤At+B for finite A,B on this ray. If a decreasing global FS sequence converged to v, its first term would majorize v and force t²≤At+B for all t≥0, impossible. This proves the printed Proposition 4.19 counterexample on a smooth affine line, without external regularization theorems.

Correcting the growth definition to an UPPER bound excludes this example, but neither proves the corrected regularization/removal nor validates all singular applications. The strict contact LF1972 also prints comparison with l(t) rather than l(t'); we do not certify its construction by changing one symbol. Complete pertinent trace, Rossi/Runge, singular-induction and descent bodies are retained in provenance, not imported as premises. Theorem 6.3 LF1926–1929 and Theorem 6.5 LF1938–1941 have countable-dense-subfield assumptions; Theorem 7.1 adds an arbitrary-field descent that also needs checking. This note disproves an indispensable proposition under its printed definition, NOT the final singular EP conclusion or any properly reconstructed corrected theorem.

notes.text:
The unchanged original all-normal-cone, all-Reeb P13.2 has not been solved. The strongest unconditional result proved in n1–n3 is: for every Radon probability μ on the fixed K=X0^T, finite explicit FS dual energy Lξ(μ) is equivalent to E1(ξ)⊂L1(μ) and is necessary for a genuine output; every such target has genuine FS approximate solutions with quantitative weak error, I-Cauchy potentials and bounded normalized energy; any actual E1 I-limit would give a genuine solution by the proved fixed-ray MA continuity estimate. Carrier usc-sup stability transfers through actual roots, including irrational fields. In cone dimension one the sole probability is realized exactly. None of these facts proves image sufficiency in dimensions ≥2.

The indispensable missing assertion for the Cauchy route is actual completeness/realization of E1(ξ)/R on every original normal cone. A formal completion or closure described using unknown outputs is not accepted as a characterization. An envelope route instead needs a verified singular normal rational envelope base; carrier transport alone supplies no such base. If using compactness and variational limits, target integration continuity for those nonmonotone limits must also be checked. Decreasing target-integral continuity proved in n1 alone does not imply it. The public singular source cannot be cited without repairing and checking the chain: n3 gives a mathematical counterexample to its lower-growth Proposition 4.19 as printed. This does not disprove its corrected final EP conclusion.
